name: mdx-setup-path
purpose: The one canonical way to stand MDx up locally, plus the opt-in production-shaped path. Cold start is a single command; the GUI takes over after a running stack.
cold_start_rule: The cold start is one command. It DETECTS prerequisites and prints exact install steps for any that are missing, but never installs them - safe on locked-down machines. Everything after a running stack happens in the GUI, not the terminal.
drift_rule: There is exactly one default local path. This contract is the single source of truth; setup-path-check enforces it against the Makefile, scripts, and QUICKSTART so the snapshot and Docker stories cannot silently re-diverge.

canonical_path.label: Local, snapshot-backed
canonical_path.for: the default - anyone standing MDx up on one machine, no database to run
steps: detect prerequisites (Rust, Node, pnpm) and print exact install steps for any missing - never auto-install
install the workspace packages the product shell needs
boot the snapshot-backed kernel and the product shell
open the browser to the first-run welcome screen

opt_in_path.label: Production-shaped (Docker + Postgres)
opt_in_path.for: rehearsing the production-shaped stack on one machine, through the deployment-profile gate

prerequisites.why: the product shell is a pnpm workspace

success: a first-run welcome screen in the browser, never a JSON file
